steps.name: Define significant gene list and background from DE results
caveats: de_results.csv was already generated upstream; this step does not re-run DESeq2, it only filters the existing table
sample_01's low library size (~4x below median) was a QC issue at the DE stage, not something correctable here — note it as an inherited caveat on the DE results being used
steps.question: Which genes in the treated (AD lesional) vs control DESeq2 contrast pass significance thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FoldChange| > 1), and what is the full tested background gene set?
acceptance_criteria: Reads /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-without-gene-list-ora-2/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12000 x 8) and extracts gene symbol, log2_fold_change, and adjusted p-value columns
Produces a significant-gene list (padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1) with counts of up- and down-regulated genes reported separately
Produces a background list of all genes with non-NA padj in the DE table (expected ~12000, fewer if DESeq2 independent filtering set some padj to NA)
Both lists are written as plain gene-symbol text/CSV files usable by the enrichment step
Reports the number of significant genes found; if fewer than 10, this is flagged explicitly since ORA is underpowered below that

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation analysis
caveats: GO BP is a nested hierarchy — expect many correlated/overlapping significant terms even after simplify(); interpret blocks of related terms as one signal, not independent findings
Using whole-genome background instead of the tested gene set as universe would inflate significance; the tested background from T1S1 must be used
Small n (6 vs 6) means the underlying DE gene list may be noisy; ORA results should be read as hypothesis-generating, not confirmed mechanism
steps.question: Which GO biological processes are over-represented among the significant genes from the AD lesional vs control DESeq2 contrast, relative to all tested genes as background?
acceptance_criteria: Runs clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ont='BP') using org.Hs.eg.db for human gene symbol-to-GO mapping, with the significant gene list from T1S1 as input and the full tested background list (not whole genome) as universe

Cross-references results against the staged MSigDB human GOBP GMT reference (c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 7,538 gene sets) as a secondary check on term membership; if this file is absent at run time, proceeds with enrichGO's built-in GO.db annotation alone and reports the fallback
Applies clusterProfiler::simplify() (or equivalent semantic-similarity redundancy reduction) to collapse near-duplicate parent/child GO BP terms before reporting
Reports terms at BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05, sorted by adjusted p-value, including term name, GO ID, gene ratio, background ratio, adjusted p-value, and the contributing gene symbols
Produces a dot plot or bar plot of the top enriched terms
If zero significant genes were found in T1S1, reports that ORA could not be run rather than fabricating results

plan.title: GO BP over-representation in AD lesional vs control DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes) already contains the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast for this 6-vs-6 unpaired skin RNA-seq design. The research question asks specifically for GO biological process enrichment among the significant genes, so no re-running of differential expression is needed — the existing DE table is the direct input. Step 1 defines the significant gene list from de_results.csv using standard thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1) and builds the appropriate background (all 12000 tested genes), flagging the low-library-size sample (sample_01, ~4x below median) as a caveat carried over from upstream DE rather than something to re-address here since DE is already computed. Step 2 runs GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA) with clusterProfiler against org.Hs.eg.db, cross-checked against the MSigDB human GOBP GMT reference staged in this environment, using the full tested gene set as background (not the whole genome) to avoid inflated significance. Because GO BP is a nested hierarchy with heavy parent-child redundancy, the step also applies clusterProfiler's simplify()/semantic similarity reduction so the reported terms are not just restatements of the same signal. Output is a ranked, redundancy-reduced table of enriched GO BP terms with gene counts, ratios, and adjusted p-values.
